interest: Shows ONI tracking Japanese travelers via Pan Am passenger records, and Guatemalan dictator Ubico's resistance to Japanese trade overtures.
overview: This file (894.20214) documents U.S. diplomatic and naval intelligence monitoring of Japanese activities in Guatemala and neighboring Central American republics between 1932 and 1940. Spurred by concerns from the Office of Naval Intelligence regarding potential espionage disguised as coastal topographical surveys and commercial fishing, American diplomats and military attachés systematically tracked Japanese vessels, diplomatic personnel, and commercial overtures. Key matters covered include suspicious, flagless ship sightings along the Pacific coast suspected of naval reconnaissance, Minister Saichiro Koshida's rebuffed 1937 attempts to secure coastal and trade concessions from President Jorge Ubico, transit records of Japanese officials and travelers via Pan American Airways, and the Guatemalan government's rejection of a 1940 coffee barter proposition by Mitsui and Company. Throughout, the documents underscore Guatemala's official distrust of Japan, its protective tariffs, and public solidarity with China during the Second Sino-Japanese War.

subfiles.about: Instruction requesting discreet investigation into reported Japanese topographical surveys and disguised fishing activities along Central American coasts.
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 167 directs Minister Sheldon Whitehouse to investigate reports of Japanese disguised as fishermen conducting coastal surveys in Guatemala, using discreet consular cooperation; identical orders went to other Central American and Mexican posts.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 167 from Department of State to Sheldon Whitehouse on Japanese Coastal Surveys
subfiles.to: Sheldon Whitehouse, American Minister to Guatemala

subfiles.about: Report confirming the absence of Japanese coastal survey activities in Guatemala and recalling a 1930 fishing concession proposal.
subfiles.from: Sheldon Whitehouse, American Minister to Guatemala
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 558: Whitehouse reports no recent Japanese activity on Guatemala's coasts, noting only a 1930 rumor of a Japanese-backed west-coast fishing concession, already reported earlier.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 558 from Sheldon Whitehouse to Secretary of State on Japanese Fishing Concession

subfiles.about: Report on suspicious, flagless vessels sighted off Guatemalan coasts suspected of Japanese naval reconnaissance.
subfiles.from: Walter H. McKinney, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 238: McKinney relays Guatemalan reports of three unidentified vessels (1936-37), believed Japanese-owned and operating from Mexico to reconnoiter Guatemala's coast for military purposes.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 238 from Walter H. McKinney to Secretary of State on Clandestine Visits of Ships

subfiles.about: Intelligence report detailing the failed diplomatic mission of Japanese Minister Saichiro Koshida and anti-Japanese sentiment in Guatemala.
subfiles.from: Frank H. Lamson-Scribner, Major, U.S. Marine Corps, Naval Attaché
subfiles.summary: Naval Attaché Lamson-Scribner reports Japan's Minister Saichiro Koshida sought Guatemalan coastal concessions and a trade treaty, both rejected by President Ubico amid Guatemalan distrust of Japan and sympathy for China.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report from Naval Attaché Lamson-Scribner on Japanese Diplomatic Mission

subfiles.about: Intelligence report tracking the air transit of Japanese national Koyaburo K. T. I. through Guatemala City to and from Panama.
subfiles.from: Frank H. Lamson-Scribner, Major, U.S. Marine Corps, Naval Attaché
subfiles.summary: ONI report tracks Japanese national Koyaburo K. T. I.'s transit through Guatemala City in September-October 1939, en route to Panama and Mexico via Pan American Airways.
subfiles.title: Attaché's Report Serial No. 434 on Transit of Koyaburo K. T. I.

subfiles.about: Intelligence report tracking regional travels of Shunichi Yamamoto and Japanese Military Attaché Yoshiaki Nishi.
subfiles.from: Frank H. Lamson-Scribner, Major, U.S. Marine Corps, Naval Attaché
subfiles.summary: Major Lamson-Scribner tracks Japanese travelers through Central America, including Military Attaché Yoshiaki Nishi, interviewed in Costa Rica despite lacking official Guatemalan accreditation.
subfiles.title: Attaché's Report Serial No. 65 on Japanese Movements in Central America and Military Attaché Yoshiaki Nishi

subfiles.about: Two-page intelligence report detailing the transit of high-ranking Japanese diplomats and travelers through Guatemala.
subfiles.from: Frank M. June, Captain, U.S. Marine Corps, Naval Attaché
subfiles.summary: Naval Attaché Capt. Frank June tracks Japanese officials' Pan Am flights through Guatemala (May-June 1940), including Minister Sotomatsu Kato's hemisphere-wide mission to promote compensation trade treaties.
subfiles.title: Attaché's Report Serial No. 213 on Japanese Diplomatic Missions and Passenger Movements

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet summarizing Guatemala's rejection of a commercial barter proposal by Mitsui and Company.
subfiles.from: Fay Allen Des Portes, American Minister to Guatemala
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch 1297: Mitsui & Co. offered to buy $250,000 of Guatemalan coffee yearly for tariff-free imports; Guatemala refused.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 1297 on Mitsui & Co. Coffee-Trade Offer
